answer: Yes. Oren receives the depth appropriate to the protagonist through his memories, grief, self-awareness, and quiet compassion. The briefly appearing figures—his father, brother, former wife, surveyor, and emergency responders—have distinctive details or attitudes that make them feel human without requiring full arcs. Even the unnamed woman’s limited characterization is purposeful: her unknowability becomes central to Oren’s encounter with mortality and his desire to acknowledge her life.
